hypotheses.claim: A research receipt may contribute to canonical routing/promotion only if its canonical tuple is validated against the current canonical and bootstrap tuple at write time and the validation identity is receipt-bound.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Canonical boot metadata is advisory; target artifact/run identity alone is sufficient.
hypotheses.discriminator: Replay identical valid target evidence with current, stale, future and unknown canonical tuples. Preserve all raw evidence, but only current/supersession-valid tuples may receive canonical routing credit.
hypotheses.falsifier: Any stale/future tuple receives canonical promotion, or a valid target result is deleted rather than preserved as noncanonical evidence.

hypotheses.claim: ProductStart safety requires closure over every executable surface before the first attested runtime guard, not merely the interpreter import graph.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Inherited shell PATH/environment is outside the ProductStart threat model because service ownership fixes it.
hypotheses.discriminator: Run the installed service and launcher under controlled PATH/helper, LD_PRELOAD, Python site/.pth, working-directory and manifest substitutions. Any pre-guard marker or unbound byte aborts before state open.
hypotheses.falsifier: Attacker-controlled pre-guard code executes while the downstream V4 receipt still passes.

hypotheses.claim: A single nominal ClayCode admission proof over the source/typed tree should dominate every backend, preventing Python and C host coercion from becoming accidental semantics.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Backend-local guards are simpler and sufficient; a shared checker creates correlated blind spots.
hypotheses.discriminator: Cross backend matrix: Bool-to-Int/Int-to-Bool call arguments, wrong return type, ambiguous variant, non-Bool condition, multi-chain and host intrinsic. Compare shared-checker-only, backend-only and both, with lesion/sabotage.
hypotheses.falsifier: Any backend executes a program rejected by the bound nominal proof, or both accept a host-coercion mutant.

hypotheses.claim: Deterministic unique-receipt folding gives exactly-once derived reward only relative to a bound, revalidated source frontier and lineage.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: A mutable transactional consumption ledger is necessary for incremental scale and causal audit.
hypotheses.discriminator: Concurrent new DONE during fold, source rollback/fork, policy change, cache resurrection/corruption and million-receipt scaling. Compare full deterministic rebuild, frontier-bound incremental fold and mutable ledger.
hypotheses.falsifier: A projection labelled current omits/duplicates a committed source event, or source rollback silently revives/removes reward.

hypotheses.claim: PR head and PR synthetic/current-main merge tree are distinct evidence identities; release integration needs both or an exact two-parent current-main receipt.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Merge-only testing exactly models the future release and makes head-only evidence redundant.
hypotheses.discriminator: Construct head-green/merge-red and head-red/merge-green controls; require receipts to state exact identity and forbid cross-identity promotion.
hypotheses.falsifier: A green run on one identity is represented as proof for the other.

hypotheses.claim: Storage runtime, startup code closure, builder provenance, exact subject/install bytes, unique state lineage, owner identity, exclusive live instance and installed restart recovery are non-substitutable ProductStart axes.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: The full AND gate is overconservative; some axes are redundant under an owner-controlled deployment channel.
hypotheses.discriminator: Authority Cut-Set Tomography: hold all but one axis green, remove or swap the remaining proof, and observe whether boot/effect/state admission still occurs.
hypotheses.falsifier: Any missing axis can be removed without changing effective authority across fresh boot, crash restart, rollback and sibling-state transplant.

hypotheses.claim: Unrelated-task switching during a nonterminal task needs one-shot consent bound to stable principal, execution epoch and exact source-task revision.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Canonical task lifecycle plus ordinary authenticated follow-up intent is sufficient; sidecar consent duplicates state.
hypotheses.discriminator: Revision advance, credential rotation with stable principal, session/client swap, crash after consume, and two concurrent consumers.
hypotheses.falsifier: Stale or replayed consent changes task authority, or legitimate same-task continuation is blocked.

novel_concepts.name: Receipt Wormhole
novel_concepts.definition: Valid evidence connected to an impossible/stale/future canonical anchor; evidence survives, promotion credit does not.

novel_concepts.name: Pre-Guard Shadow Cone
novel_concepts.definition: The transitive set of shell helpers, loaders, environment hooks and path resolutions that can execute before the first attested runtime guard.

novel_concepts.name: Host-Coercion Wormhole
novel_concepts.definition: A typed source crosses an unchecked call/return boundary and re-enters after the host silently converts its value.

novel_concepts.name: Projection Ghost
novel_concepts.definition: A reward event disappears or reappears because source lineage/frontier, policy and derived cache are not jointly bound.

novel_concepts.name: Authority Cut-Set Tomography
novel_concepts.definition: Lesion one proof axis at a time while all others remain green to identify which evidence actually controls boot/effect/state authority.
